doc.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: Favourite albums: Harold Land, Something More, Sphere and Mwandishi
summary: He names albums he still likes, including A New Shade of Blue, his own CDs, the Sphere albums and Herbie Hancock's Mwandishi and The Prisoner.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You said something that I really found interesting early on, referring to your own album you did that became “Something More” but you continued to like it. Could you pick out what would be ten albums that you would continue to like from your discography?
Well I mean of anybody you’ve played with.
Oh okay. Harold Land “A New Shade of Blue.”
I have it next door, you have to sign it.
It’s one of my favorite albums.
Mine, that’s “Something More.” In fact I seem to like all my CDs now that I did.

And I’ve been very fortunate, I’ve been able to put out at least one or two a year. After that dry period between 1987 and 1996, but since 1996 I’ve got new product coming out all the time. “A New Shade of Blue,” “Something More,” those Sphere Albums.
With Charlie Rouse and Kenny Barron and Ben Riley. Oh I don’t know.
How about something with Herbie? Anything in particular? © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
Yeah the “Mwandishi.” I think we did about five or six, something like that.
There was some nice writing on those things.
Mmm. Oh yeah. “The Prisoner.” Oh Herbie did some of his best writing on that.
